questions.q: Why does aligning fundamental data onto a daily price series create a feature-engineering challenge?
options: Fundamentals are reported quarterly with a reporting lag, while price updates daily, so a naive join can leak a value before it was actually knowable
Fundamental data is always more accurate than price data
Price data cannot be stored in the same DataFrame as fundamental data
Fundamentals never change over time
questions.explain: Fundamentals update on a quarterly, lagged schedule while price updates daily; joining them naively on the quarter-end date (rather than the actual report date) would give a daily feature access to information before it was publicly known.

questions.q: In the worked example, why did the naive forward-fill show EPS = 1.05 starting on 2023-06-30, even though that value wasn't actually reported until 2023-08-04?
options: Because the naive join used the quarter-end date as the join key instead of the actual report date, leaking the new value 25 trading days early
Because EPS of 1.05 was the correct value for the entire year
Because pandas automatically corrects for reporting lags
Because the price series had a data error
questions.explain: The naive approach forward-filled the EPS value from the quarter-end date, which is weeks before the earnings were actually released on 2023-08-04 -- a 25-trading-day leakage window identified in the comparison table.

questions.q: What does `pd.merge_asof(..., direction='backward')` do that makes it the correct tool for point-in-time fundamental joins?
options: It joins each price row to the most recent fundamental observation whose timestamp is at or before that row's own timestamp
It averages all fundamental values across the entire dataset
It joins each price row to the next future fundamental observation
It deletes all rows without a matching fundamental value
questions.explain: merge_asof with direction='backward' finds, for each row, the latest earlier (or equal) timestamped value in the other series -- exactly the point-in-time guarantee needed so a feature never sees data from after its own timestamp.

questions.q: Why is alternative data (news sentiment, web traffic, satellite imagery, etc.) often attractive as a feature source?
options: It is always free and has decades of history
It is often orthogonal to price-derived signals and some sources update faster than quarterly fundamentals
It requires no point-in-time discipline at all
It eliminates the need for any traditional price or fundamental data
questions.explain: Alternative data doesn't suffer the price-derived collinearity problem from Lesson 29, and some sources (web traffic, search trends) update closer to daily, faster than quarterly fundamentals.

questions.q: Which of the following is a real practical problem with alternative data, as discussed in this lesson?
options: It is immune to overfitting because it has so much history
Vendor survivorship bias, short history, high cost, and noisy/sparse coverage
It cannot be joined onto a price series using any pandas function
It is always more predictive than fundamental data
questions.explain: Alternative data brings real practical issues: data vendors that stop operating are often the ones whose signal didn't work (survivorship bias), many datasets have only a few years of history, institutional-grade data can be expensive, and coverage is often sparse and noisy.
